items.title: AI Platform: Memory, Tools, Guardrails, Observability, Shipping a Production Agent - Dewang Sultania
items.summary: In this talk, Dewang Sultania, ML Engineer at Netflix and co-author of Designing AI Systems, shares his technical journey from building early inference platforms at Adobe to deploying multimodal AI models at scale. We explore the complete architecture of enterprise AI platforms, focusing on evaluation datasets, tool calling orchestration, and the practical realities of shipping production agents. You’ll learn about: - The essential components needed to build an enterprise AI platform from scratch - How traditional software engineers can transition into AI platform engineering - The critical technical differences between session management and LLM memory - Strategies for building, versioning, and trusting custom evaluation datasets - Optimizing LLM tool calling and selecting the right performance benchmarks - When to use multi-agent architectures versus single-agent systems - Techniques for overcoming the lost in the middle problem in RAG pipelines TIMECODES: 00:00 Core Components of Enterprise AI Platforms 11:46 Career Path to AI Platform Engineering 18:33 Session Management Versus LLM Memory Management 26:47 Best Practices for Custom LLM Evaluation Datasets 32:28 LLM Tool Calling Optimization and Benchmark Selection 39:25 Context Window Limits and AI Agent Tool Scaling 45:37 Single-Agent Versus Multi-Agent System Architecture 52:16 LLM-as-a-Judge Alignment and Human Evaluation Strategies 58:11 Solutions for the Lost in the Middle Problem in RAG Systems 01:03:27 Designing AI Systems Book Announcement This discussion is perfect for software engineers, machine learning practitioners, and technical leaders building real-world AI applications. It offers practical insights for anyone transitioning into AI platform engineering or tasked with scaling LLM features for enterprise production. In this talk, Dewang Sultania, ML Engineer at Netflix and co-author of Designing AI Systems, shares his technical journey from building early inference platforms at Adobe to deploying multimodal AI models at scale. We explore the complete architecture of enterprise AI platforms, focusing on evaluation datasets, tool calling orchestration, and the practical realities of shipping production agents.


You’ll learn about:

- The essential components needed to build an enterprise AI platform from scratch

- How traditional software engineers can transition into AI platform engineering

- The critical technical differences between session management and LLM memory

- Strategies for building, versioning, and trusting custom evaluation datasets

- Optimizing LLM tool calling and selecting the right performance benchmarks

- When to use multi-agent architectures versus single-agent systems

- Techniques for overcoming the lost in the middle problem in RAG pipelines


TIMECODES:

00:00 Core Components of Enterprise AI Platforms

11:46 Career Path to AI Platform Engineering

18:33 Session Management Versus LLM Memory Management

26:47 Best Practices for Custom LLM Evaluation Datasets

32:28 LLM Tool Calling Optimization and Benchmark Selection

39:25 Context Window Limits and AI Agent Tool Scaling

45:37 Single-Agent Versus Multi-Agent System Architecture

52:16 LLM-as-a-Judge Alignment and Human Evaluation Strategies

58:11 Solutions for the Lost in the Middle Problem in RAG Systems

01:03:27 Designing AI Systems Book Announcement


This discussion is perfect for software engineers, machine learning practitioners, and technical leaders building real-world AI applications. It offers practical insights for anyone transitioning into AI platform engineering or tasked with scaling LLM features for enterprise production.

items.title: Is This the Cheapest Way to Use AI in 2026? (65+ Models Tested) | Iskander Malikov, Trioma
items.summary: What if you didn't have to choose between ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, and instead, the platform chose for you? That's the core idea behind Trioma, a vertically integrated AI ecosystem built by Iskander and his team in the UAE. Craig Smith sits down with Iskander Malikov, Co-founder & CEO of Trioma, to unpack how Trioma's orchestration engine routes prompts across 65 models, why token price is a misleading metric, and how their GPU network lets users participate in AI infrastructure build-out to offset their own compute costs. The conversation goes deep on the economics of AI subscriptions, the coming collapse of traditional SaaS, and why Trioma believes AI should be sovereign, accessible, and community-driven, not locked behind a single company's walled garden. If you're thinking about where AI access, cost, and infrastructure are heading, this one is essential listening. Subscribe to Eye on A.I. for weekly conversations with the people building and deploying the future of AI.

items.title: Modernizing Enterprise GRC for Continuous Assurance - with Craig Unger of Hyperproof
items.summary: Shifting regulations and siloed risk and compliance functions are forcing enterprise leaders to rethink audit-driven compliance. In this episode, Craig Unger, CEO and Founder at Hyperproof, explains why compliance should be treated as a continuous state, with every control tied back to the organization's overall risk profile. He also covers standardizing a single set of controls across frameworks and regions, expressing risk in financial terms for boards, and using a five-stage maturity model to plan next steps. This episode is sponsored by Hyperproof Learn how leading organizations approach AI investment more like a venture portfolio, and why interdisciplinary collaboration is critical to defining the right data for AI success, download our free PDF report, "Beginning with AI," at emerj.com/aik1
